DIN map: Bosch 'Micro Relays' catalog 2007/2008, 'Comparison of terminal designations, Micro relay / Mini relay', pp. 2-10 of https://dalroad.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/05/Bosch-Micro-Relays.pdf (1=86 +, 2=85 -, 3=30, 4=87a, 5=87)
TE micro ISO relay V23074.note: View = relay terminal (bottom) side, i.e. the relay's mating face. This is the same orientation as the socket seen from its wire side; the socket's mating face is the mirror. 4 (87a) only on changeover types. The Bosch Micro relay A catalog (https://www.dalroad.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/05/Bosch-Micro-Relays-A.pdf p.2) cross-lists Bosch 0 986 332 010 = Tyco V23074-A1001-X007, so the Bosch table applies to this footprint. Diode types: the TE schematic puts the cathode at 1, so 1 must be +12 V (86).

TE HCR150 V23132-A2001-B200.source: Layout: TE 'High Current Relay 150' datasheet, bottom view, https://datasheet.chipsmall.com/1393315-2/330775.pdf. DIN map: ISO->DIN table in the Bosch Micro Relays catalog (above): 3=30, 5=87, 1/2 = coil.
TE HCR150 V23132-A2001-B200.note: View = terminal (bottom) side. Coil plug 1 (top) / 2 (bottom) at the left; M6 studs 5 (middle) and 3 (right). B200 = 1 form A with a coil resistor, so 1/2 are polarity-free (86/85 assignment is nominal). There is NO 4 / 87a terminal.
